evidence.curator_note: TEXT ON THE PAGE: 'The proximity of two aromatic rings leads to very facile displacement decompositions such as the one in Equation 8.109 (Schubert, Grützmacher 1980).' WHAT THE BOOK DRAWS: the precursor is 1-(2-halophenyl)-1-(2-pyridyl)ethylene enclosed in square brackets with '+.' outside the bracket - i.e. the charge and odd electron are assigned to the WHOLE molecule, not to a drawn atom. The reaction arrow is labelled '- X.'. The product is the tetracyclic ring-closed cation: the pyridine nitrogen is now bonded to the benzene carbon that carried X, creating a five-membered ring (benzene ipso C - C(=CH2) - pyridine C2 - N - benzene ortho C), the exocyclic =CH2 is retained, and a bare '+' is printed under the nitrogen. ARC COUNT (convention D): Book draws 0 arc(s). There is NO curved arrow, fishhook or barb in Equation 8.109; only the two structures and the '- X.' arrow label are printed. All three encoded moves <1,2,3> are therefore IMPLICIT, supplied by the curator for electron balance and not drawn on the page: <1> the nitrogen's odd electron into the forming N-C2 bond, <2> one electron of the breaking C2-X sigma bond into that same forming bond, <3> the second electron of the C2-X bond onto X, which is what makes the X. that the arrow label names. This 'radical site attacks, radical leaves' bookkeeping is the section's rd (radical-site displacement) pattern, the same one drawn explicitly with fishhooks in Equation 8.108 immediately above; the book leaves it implicit here. LOCALIZATION (conventions B and C): because the '+.' sits outside the bracket the curator had to localize it. The odd electron is placed in the nitrogen n orbital ([N+:9] carrying one sigma bond to C14 and one double bond to C10 = one unpaired electron in RDKit), which is both the lowest-IE site of the molecule and the atom that must attack, so move <1> has a real origin. KEKULE CHOICE: the two rings are written in exactly the Kekule form the book draws - in the pyridine the double bond runs from N to the SUBSTITUTED carbon (N9=C10, then C11=C12 and C13=C14), and in the benzene the double bond lies along the C1=C2 bond that becomes the ring-fusion bond (then C3=C4 and C5=C6). The identical bond orders are kept in the product, so the only bond changes intended by the step are the C2-Br cleavage and the N9-C2 formation; no ring is deliberately re-kekulized. VALIDATOR ARTEFACT (expected, soft): the arrow check nevertheless reports six '(soft) (aromatic/delocalised)' +/-0.5 bond-order notes on the six pyridine ring bonds (maps 9-10, 10-11, 11-12, 12-13, 13-14, 9-14). They are a perception artefact, not a missing arrow: RDKit refuses to aromatize the n-ionized precursor ring (an N+ carrying an unpaired electron) and keeps the written Kekule orders 1/2, but it does aromatize the closed-shell N-aryl pyridinium of the product to uniform order 1.5, so every ring bond appears to move by half an order. No electron moves are missing - the six deltas sum to zero around the ring. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the figure writes only 'X' and the prose never names the halogen, so X = Br is a CURATOR CHOICE made to give computable masses (with X = Cl the precursor would be 215.0496 instead, and the product ion is unchanged at 180.0802 either way). MS CONTEXT (convention G): page 215 names no ionization or activation method and no electron energy; the reacting species is the whole-molecule odd-electron radical cation drawn in brackets with '+.', so ms_context uses the convention-G molecular-ion default (EI, adduct [M]+., 70 eV). The 70 eV figure is the book's standing convention, NOT a number printed on this page.

NO MØD rule is cross-linked. rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.109' key (its chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only, German-edition numbering). The displacement rules were CHECKED against this record's instantiated precursor, not assumed (convention E). (i) IMS_4_42_rd, DFS '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[Cl+.]6>>[C.]1.[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[Cl+]6{-}2', is the closest thing in the rule base: it closes a FIVE-membered ring by attack of the radical site on the carbon four atoms away, which is the same ring size as the closure drawn here (N9-C10-C7-C1-C2). It still cannot fire: the rule hard-wires the radical site to CHLORINE and the leaving group to CARBON, i.e. the two roles are exactly swapped relative to Equation 8.109, where nitrogen attacks and a halogen leaves; and every bond in its pattern is a single bond, whereas the chain here is aromatic/olefinic (N9=C10, C7=CH2 exocyclic with C1=C2 in the ring). RDKit confirms zero matches for '[#6]~[#6]~[#6]~[#6]~[#6]~[Cl]' (no chlorine in the substrate at all). (ii) 'substituion' in IMS_bookCover.py, DFS '[_A]1[C]2[C]3[_A+.]4>>[_A.]1.[C]2[C]3[_A+]4{-}2' (live via the 'rearrangements' export, IMS_bookCover.py:484), has the right role assignment but closes a THREE-membered ring, not the five-membered ring drawn here, and its two '_A' slots are the same MØD term variable and therefore unify to one element, whereas the attacking atom is N and the leaving atom is a halogen. Its single-bond backbone also fails on this substrate: '[Br]-[#6]-[#6]-[#6]' -> 0 matches (the Br-bearing carbon sits on the C1=C2 double bond); only the bond-order-agnostic form '[Br]~[#6]~[#6]~[#6]' matches (3 hits), which is not what the DFS demands. CONCLUSION: the aryl/heteroaryl proximity displacements of Section 8.11 are entirely unrepresented in the MØD rule base; encoding them needs ring-protected, bond-order-agnostic rules with independent element slots (the same requirement noted for the aromatic-fragmentation rules elsewhere in the project).

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (convention F): page 215 prints no m/z and no abundance for Equation 8.109; the halogen is left generic as 'X'. The product species is therefore detected=false and the peak assignment has status 'inferred' with relative_intensity omitted. The masses are curator-computed monoisotopic m/z (RDKit ExactMolWt, electron-mass corrected) for the CHOSEN instantiation X = Br (79Br): M+. C13H10BrN+. 258.9986 -> ring-closed cation C13H10N+ 180.0802 + Br. 78.9183. The precursor m/z depends on that arbitrary choice (X = Cl would give 215.0496); the product ion m/z 180.0802 does not, since X is lost.
